milestones.claim: IBM reports measuring accurate expectation values on a noisy 127-qubit processor for circuits with up to 60 layers of two-qubit gates (2,880 CNOT gates), and states this is evidence for “the utility of quantum computing in a pre-fault-tolerant era”.

evidence.quote: Here we report experiments on a noisy 127-qubit processor and demonstrate the measurement of accurate expectation values for circuit volumes at a scale beyond brute-force classical computation. We argue that this represents evidence for the utility of quantum computing in a pre-fault-tolerant era.
We use a superconducting quantum processor with 127 qubits to run quantum circuits with up to 60 layers of two-qubit gates, a total of 2,880 CNOT gates.

milestones.claim: IBM researchers report a family of quantum low-density parity-check codes with an error threshold of 0.7% under a standard circuit-based noise model, and estimate that 12 encoded qubits can be preserved for nearly 1 million syndrome cycles using 288 physical qubits at a 0.1% physical error rate (a protocol and simulation result, not a hardware experiment).

evidence.quote: Our approach achieves an error threshold of 0.7% for the standard circuit-based noise model, on par with the surface code

In particular, we show that 12 logical qubits can be preserved for nearly 1 million syndrome cycles using 288 physical qubits in total, assuming the physical error rate of 0.1%, whereas the surface code would require nearly 3,000 physical qubits to achieve said performance.

milestones.claim: IBM releases the 133-qubit Heron processor via the cloud and begins operating its first IBM Quantum System Two in Yorktown Heights, New York, with three Heron processors.

milestones.claim: IBM and University of Chicago researchers report a 64-qubit, depth-73 Clifford circuit doped with 314 T gates, encoded in spacetime codes on 76 physical qubits, with a certified fidelity lower bound of 0.349 at 95% confidence; IBM's release states the work achieves the criteria for “quantum advantage”.

evidence.quote: We demonstrate our proposal with a $64$-qubit, depth-$73$ Clifford circuit, doped with $314$ $T$ gates. We use a total of $76$ physical qubits to encode this computation in spacetime codes, effectively suppressing gate error rates by $10\times$ after syndrome post-selection, and yielding a state with a fidelity lower bound of $0.349$ with $95\%$ confidence.
today announced a demonstration in quantum computing that achieves the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage

milestones.claim: Google reports sampling one instance of a 53-qubit random quantum circuit a million times in about 200 seconds on Sycamore, estimates approximately 10,000 years for a state-of-the-art classical supercomputer, and describes the result as “an experimental realization of quantum supremacy” for this task.

evidence.quote: Our Sycamore processor takes about 200 seconds to sample one instance of a quantum circuit a million times—our benchmarks currently indicate that the equivalent task for a state-of-the-art classical supercomputer would take approximately 10,000 years. This dramatic increase in speed compared to all known classical algorithms is an experimental realization of quantum supremacy
to create quantum states on 53 qubits

milestones.claim: Google reports a distance-5 surface-code encoded qubit whose logical error per cycle (2.914%) is modestly lower on average than an ensemble of distance-3 encodings (3.028%).

evidence.quote: We find that our distance-5 surface code logical qubit modestly outperforms an ensemble of distance-3 logical qubits on average, in terms of both logical error probability over 25 cycles and logical error per cycle ((2.914 ± 0.016)% compared to (3.028 ± 0.023)%).
In 2023, we announced the first-ever experimental demonstration that it is possible to scale quantum error correction (Milestone 2).
evidence.locator: section 'Our progress towards building a quantum computer'

milestones.claim: Google reports two surface-code memories on Willow processors, with logical error suppressed by a factor of 2.14 per code-distance increase of 2 and a 101-qubit distance-7 code at 0.143% error per cycle, and describes them as “below-threshold surface code memories”.

evidence.quote: Here we present two below-threshold surface code memories on our newest generation of superconducting processors, Willow: a distance-7 code and a distance-5 code integrated with a real-time decoder. The logical error rate of our larger quantum memory is suppressed by a factor of Λ = 2.14 ± 0.02 when increasing the code distance by 2, culminating in a 101-qubit distance-7 code with 0.143% ± 0.003 per cent error per cycle of error correction.
An Author Correction to this article was published on 28 April 2026

milestones.claim: Researchers from Alice & Bob and collaborators report a superconducting cat qubit with bit-flip times exceeding 10 s and phase-flip times greater than 490 ns, with phase control that did not break the bit-flip protection.

Most importantly, we controlled the phase of these quantum superpositions without breaking the bit-flip protection.
